name: Google Compute Engine A3 / A3 Ultra (NVIDIA H100 and H200)
region: us-central1 (prices as published); a3 and a3-ultragpu offered across us-east1/4/5, us-west, europe-west, asia-northeast
price_basis: per GPU-hour. a3-highgpu-8g = 8x H100 at $88.490000119/instance-hr / 8 = $11.0613. a3-megagpu-8g = 8x H100 at $93.400712807/8 = $11.6751. a3-ultragpu-8g = 8x H200 at $84.806908493/8 = $10.6009. Prices are the us-central1 column as published 2026-10-03.
notes: THE MOST EXPENSIVE ON-DEMAND H100 HOUR IN THE ENTIRE SLICE - $11.06/GPU-hour against $3.29 for the cheapest single H100 (Lambda) and $6.88 for AWS on-demand. Two caveats that cut the other way. First, the page's 1-year and 3-year CUD columns for a3-highgpu-8g render in an order that makes the 1-year figure ($61.38) look HIGHER than a plausible on-demand relationship and the 3-year figure ($38.86) far lower; the column ordering in the rendered table is ambiguous, so treat the CUD numbers as suspect and only the on-demand column as solid. Second, Google states accelerator-optimized machines are NOT eligible for sustained use discounts or flexible committed use discounts - only resource-based CUDs apply. So the discount path on A3 is narrower than the headline suggests. Regional spread is not visible in this page: the region selector ships with us-central1 preselected and requesting ?region=us-east4 returned byte-identical figures, so the page did not honour the parameter server-side and no regional comparison should be drawn from it. Access requires a reservation in practice, not just quota: A3 capacity has historically been allocation-only. Important structural note: the on-demand price is bundled with vCPU, RAM AND bundled Local SSD (a3-highgpu-8g carries 6,000 GiB), which is why the per-GPU figure looks bad next to a bare neocloud GPU - you are not paying for a GPU alone.
